title: Something Borrowed, Something Spewed

panels.action: Wide hotel entrance, dressed for the wedding. Tony carries the secured, switched-off backpack jetter. Sean has the long-handled plunger and service kit. Guests are already arriving. Story title: Something Borrowed, Something Spewed. Include a small inset pop-out of BJ accompanying his radio speech, using his established AI/server-rack design. Make his artificial nature visually clear. This is a view of the remote speaker, not BJ physically present at the hotel. Sean’s plunger is secured cup-side-up, handle down, in the reviewed back carrier or approved tool-belt alternative; his hand carries the service kit.
dialogue: The hotel kitchen has lost water pressure. Dinner service starts in twenty minutes.

panels.action: At the entrance mat, they set their equipment down and put on white boot covers. Sean watches guests being shown to their reception tables. He is trying to work out how the job can fit into the time they have.
dialogue: They’re already seating people for dinner. How are we supposed to fix it if we don't even know what's wrong?

panels.action: Tony answers while fitting his other boot cover. His manner is relaxed and matter-of-fact: this is familiar job pressure, and he has time to explain his approach. Allow room for a complete thought, potentially in two linked balloons.
dialogue: Same way we do any job. Find out what's happening, find out what changed, then work back from there. They'll want a time. Don't give them one just to make them feel better.

panels.action: Both have their boot covers on and have picked up their equipment. Tony checks the job notes on his phone. Sean looks toward the wedding guests as the manager approaches. The plunger is stowed cup-side-up, handle down, with credible weight support and restraints against tipping and swinging; the service kit is carried by hand.
dialogue: Right. I was about to tell them we'd have it sorted by the first course.
We'll do what we can for them. That's all we can promise.

panels.action: Their covered boots meet the manager's polished shoes at the cream carpet. The radio interrupts just before the manager can speak. Include a small inset pop-out of BJ accompanying his radio speech, using his established AI/server-rack design. Make his artificial nature visually clear. This is a view of the remote speaker, not BJ physically present at the hotel.
dialogue: They’ve approved the emergency rate. Take your time.

panels.action: The manager leads them beside the ballroom. He keeps smiling at passing guests while trying to talk privately to Tony. Sean follows with the tools. The wedding is for a very high-paying client. The manager is extremely stressed and determined that every detail follow the plan; his courtesy to guests is strained.
dialogue: Thank God you're here. The chef just tried to rinse his hands in a champagne bucket. Now the upstairs taps are going too.

panels.action: They reach the service door. A wet towel has been pushed against its bottom edge. The manager positions himself as if to keep walking past it; Tony has stopped. Give this conversational panel room.
dialogue: This morning. There was a small leak, but that was dealt with. We've just had the place refurbished. I can't have people thinking—
What was done to the leak?

panels.action: Water is escaping around the towel toward a connected power strip and tangled cables. Its lead reaches a wall socket; the indicator is lit. Sean stops on dry carpet and gives Tony a worried, incredulous look. He points without touching anything. His voice is small.

Tony's distracted scan stops at the hazard Sean has spotted. Both remain on the dry side. Tony turns to the manager; Sean sets the kit down clear of the wet area and stands where he can stop passing staff from walking into it.
dialogue: Keep people away from this doorway. Get maintenance down here. We need this circuit isolated and checked before anyone goes near that water.
Right. Yes. Just—please don't switch off the whole ballroom.

panels.action: The manager makes the call on his mobile. From the dry side, Tony shines his torch through the opened cupboard door. Sean watches the corridor beside the safely placed kit, plunger in hand. The repair is still outside the reader’s view.
dialogue: I need you at the service cupboard. Now.
It was supposed to last through the reception.

panels.action: The answer to Who did the repair? fills the panel: a split pipe buried in gray duct tape, wet edges peeling away and a thin stream escaping between them. Beside it, the manager sweats and attempts a sickly, nervous smile while tucking the matching roll into his jacket. The roll remains plainly visible.

Sean looks at Tony: the roll has explained everything to him. Tony holds the manager's gaze. The manager's strained smile is beginning to fail. This is shared recognition, not another close-up of the pipe.

Tony addresses the manager directly from the dry threshold. He has assessed the repair and is setting out what they need to do. He is firm and practical, without humiliating the manager. Give the exchange sufficient room; Tony’s speech may use two connected balloons.
dialogue: We're going to stop the water, then fix this properly. While we're doing that, you can show me anything else that's been patched up. Where's the main water shutoff?
Downstairs, in the basement mechanical room. I—

panels.action: Every toilet in the nearby bathroom flushes at once, cutting him off. All three turn toward the bathroom, which is reached along the dry corridor, away from the electrical hazard. The manager hesitates over his answer; this new disturbance is undermining his efforts to keep the wedding on plan. A simple RESTROOM CLOSED placard hangs flat on the door by a short cord. Everyone remains in the foreground with no contact with the background door or sign.

At the bathroom threshold, they look into a row of closed stalls. Tony aims his torch into the room; the jetter nozzle remains secured and switched off. Sean has left the service kit against the dry corridor wall, clear of the exit, and carries the plunger. A small ripple spreads beneath one stall. Hold the silence. Neither is posed for combat or anticipating a monster; the creature remains unseen until the page turn. The door-mounted sign moves with the door when opened. The restroom is well lit; Tony has no flashlight in hand and casts no flashlight beam.

Large reveal, approximately half the page: the Flushfiend smashes through its stall door. Ceramic teeth, pipe legs, flying fragments. Tony and Sean are caught equally off guard: both stare for a beat, then set themselves to meet it. Sean raises the plunger in both hands; Tony brings the jetter nozzle to bear. They stand shoulder to shoulder at the threshold. Neither has seen anything like this before. The jetter has not fired. Show neighboring stall partitions and bathroom fixtures. The separate intact bathroom entrance door is visible at the threshold; it is not the broken stall door. The entrance opens outward into the corridor, with hinges on the right when viewed from the corridor. Preserve this swing across the sequence.

The manager stumbles into the corridor and catches sight of the reception guests at the ballroom doors. His polished manner is gone. Tony turns just enough to shout to him while Sean keeps his eyes on the creature and covers the bathroom entrance. Arrange the speakers for this reading order. Existing corridor furniture stays against the wall. Sean has normal, clearly connected shoulder, elbow, wrist and hand anatomy.
dialogue: Get everyone out of this corridor! Now!

panels.action: Sean has just crossed the threshold. His plunger rests against the corridor wall. Catch him mid-turn, snapping the door shut with his right palm flat on the door while his eyes stay on the creature through the narrowing gap. His jaw is tight, his shoulders high. His left arm hangs naturally as he calls. The door swings freely on its established right-side hinges. The impact comes after it closes.
The entrance clicks shut. Tony secures his nozzle and steps in beside Sean. Both put their hands on the same closed door. The knob is mounted on its latch edge.
Something heavy hits the other side. Sean feels it first through his shoulder. Tony plants his boot and leans in beside him. The door holds.
A ceramic tooth punches through the wood between them, clear of their hands and faces. Both turn toward the tooth and keep their weight against the door. The plunger stays set aside.

character_context.manager: This wedding is for a very high-paying client. He is extremely stressed, determined that everything follow the plan, and increasingly nervous as events escape his control. His concealed tape repair is accompanied by an attempted sickly nervous smile, not a guilty grin.

physical_art_review.owner: Comic independently reviews every panel and adjacent-panel continuity before acceptance or display; Art self-checks before handoff.
physical_art_review.references: Establish shared character, room and prop references before panel generation. Record relative dimensions, construction and attachment points; use the same references for every appearance.
physical_art_review.scale: Keep established door width-to-height, chair seat width-to-depth, leg and back lengths, tool lengths and object-to-character scale fixed. Perspective may change their projected appearance, never their physical construction.
physical_art_review.composition: Fit camera, framing and poses around fixed objects. Never widen a single door, stretch furniture or lengthen tools to fit people or lettering. Reblock or add a panel if space is insufficient.
physical_art_review.geometry: Trace corners, straight members, seat plane, four leg attachments and continuous back posts. Check consistent perspective and occlusion, floor contact, hardware mounted on the moving door leaf, hinge side and swing direction.
physical_art_review.action: Match effort to resistance and show plausible contact and force direction. Sean and Tony brace the same closed door together. Preserve hands safely away from the breach.
physical_art_review.checks: Inspect raw panels at full resolution and assembled page at reading size. Compare neighboring panels for proportions, hardware, props, costume, anatomy and sequential action. Check the whole image after every local correction.
physical_art_review.rejection: Reject a candidate if fixing one element warps another. Do not approve staging with known structural defects to fix later. Art reports actual unresolved defects; Comic reinspects replacements.
physical_art_review.current_hold: Current four-page proof awaits identity, carrier, gesture, footwear, nozzle and palette corrections. The two-person door hold supersedes the chair-brace studies.
